title: OpenData: public data, made usable for AI agents
slideTitles: Data, made usable for the agent era.
Agents can query any data that is clean and in a database. Almost no public data is.
Every dataset we clean joins the Dataset Graph.
Infrastructure as code, written by agents.
Two tests, ten districts, one contradiction.
They had the data. They could not get at it.
The catalog is the base. The tools are the product.
Companies already sell usable public data.
Two Mac Minis run production. Disk fills first.
Verifiability is what converts the skeptics.
Every dataset discoverable. Every claim verifiable.

states.lead: Twenty-nine files. No headers. No changelog.
states.body: About 7,691 unnamed fields per row, and the salary field alone has sat in 14 different columns.

states.lead: We reconcile it once. One dataset, one query.
states.body: Every file mapped onto one schema and published as a single dataset.

states.lead: 969 datasets. 203 agencies. 1.6 billion rows.
states.body: Every square is one dataset OpenData agents cleaned and published.

states.lead: 17 categories, four of them most of the catalog.
states.body: Education, government, health and economics are 566 of the 952.

states.lead: 952 datasets. 3,291 relationships.
states.body: 952 of the 969 are ready and linked. The graph is how an agent sees the connections.

states.lead: Seven weeks, and the graph grew by half.
states.body: 630 datasets and 2,135 links in July; 952 and 3,291 today.

states.lead: A dataset is a YAML file in git.
states.body: Source, schema, transforms, checks, refresh schedule, reviewed like code. Push to main, live in about 4 minutes.

states.lead: One gate decides if the new file ships.
states.body: Every check runs against the staged file. A failure leaves yesterday’s data serving and tells us why.

states.lead: Agents wrote 93 of them in one week.
states.body: The first dataset landed 3 weeks in. Claude Code agents wrote most of the 232 added in the last four weeks.

states.lead: Two steps still need a person.
states.body: Someone starts the agent and pushes its YAML. Wire those two links and a request lands unattended.

states.lead: Roma is 90% low-income and triples Austin.
states.body: Economically disadvantaged students meeting grade level on STAAR math, 2024-25.

states.lead: Austin is last of the ten.
states.body: 22% of Austin's low-income students met grade level; Roma's 64% is nearly triple.

states.lead: The SAT flips it.
states.body: Same low-income students, same year. Three Valley districts beat Austin on the SAT, three trail it.

states.lead: STAAR and the SAT disagree.
states.body: One of these tests is measuring something that college readiness does not follow from.

states.lead: 6 of 30, without OpenData.
states.body: Sonnet 5, one fresh chat per question, web search and a sandbox. Single run.

states.lead: 25 of 30, with it.
states.body: Same model, same questions, same day. Single run per arm.

states.lead: The clock went the same way.
states.body: Median 63 seconds per chat without it, 35 with. 30 chats, totalled on stage.

states.lead: Without it, the model rebuilds the pipeline.
states.body: It spun up a sandbox in 17 of 30 chats, downloading source files to re-implement the work.

states.lead: The same shape in a bare API agent.
states.body: Same model, same prompt, only the tool list differs. This run billed per token.

states.lead: One catalog, one graph, one interface.
states.body: Everything we clean lands in one place, linked to everything like it, behind a single query layer.

states.lead: Three ways in, for three kinds of user.
states.body: Developers build on the API. Non-technical users ask an agent. Editors get charts they can edit.

states.lead: The same stack runs on private data.
states.body: Every enterprise conversation asks for it. It ships once signed demand covers the SOC 2 cost.

states.lead: Four tiers, three of them paid.
states.body: The engine is open source. The API, the agent interface and the charts are what we sell.

states.lead: AccuWeather makes $225M a year on free feeds.
states.body: The National Weather Service data underneath it costs nothing to download.

states.lead: GovWin charges $12K to $42K a seat.
states.body: The bid notices underneath are public. Both companies charge for making free data usable.

states.lead: Production is two Mac Minis on a desk.
states.body: One serves, one processes. We own the hardware, pay no cloud bill, and have 16 GB of RAM on each.

states.lead: Disk runs out long before CPU or RAM.
states.body: 105 of 150 GB used at idle, CPU load 0.11 on 8 cores. Crawler agents are blocked on storage.

states.lead: 1,104 QPS before latency moves.
states.body: Zero failures to 1,397 req/s. The wall was the proxy's memory cap, not the hardware.

states.lead: The first cloud spend is storage.
states.body: Same containers, same YAML, more disk. That unblocks the request loop and the crawler agents.

states.lead: 1M+ reads, and none of them engineers.
states.body: Data stories built on the catalog pulled 1M+ views. The readers were journalists, economists and researchers.

states.lead: Every conversation lands on the same worry.
states.body: State agencies, newsrooms, enterprises. Interest everywhere, and one question each time: does the AI make numbers up?

states.lead: So verifiability is the product.
states.body: Every answer traces to a query you can rerun. That is what a skeptic will trust.
